# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 6 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 1QH (Cave 1), Col. 6 | **Condition:** Better preserved

---

**6:1** I thank You, O Lord, for You have sustained me with Your strength and Your holy spirit You have poured upon me.

**6:2** I shall not waver. And You have strengthened me before the battles of wickedness.

**6:3** And in all their destruction You have not let me be dismayed from Your covenant.

**6:4** You have set me as a strong tower, as a high wall, and You have established my building upon rock.

**6:5** And eternal foundations for my base, and all my walls are a tested rampart that shall not be shaken.

**6:6** And You, O my God, have appointed me for the weary as a holy counsel, and You have established me in Your covenant.

**6:7** And my tongue is as one taught by You. But there is no word for the spirit of destruction.

**6:8** And no reply for all the children of guilt, for lying lips shall be struck dumb.

**6:9** For all those who attack me for judgment, You shall condemn them, to separate through me the righteous from the wicked.

**6:10** For You know every purpose of a deed and every answer of the tongue You discern.

**6:11** And You have established my heart by Your teachings and by Your truth, to direct my steps to the paths of righteousness.

**6:12** To walk before You in the land of the living, in paths of glory and peace without end.

**6:13** And without ceasing, and it is known [...] and apart from Your will nothing shall be.

**6:14** I have leaned upon Your covenant-faithfulness and upon the abundance of Your mercies.

**6:15** For You atone for iniquity and purify man from guilt by Your righteousness.

**6:16** Not for the sake of man, but for Your glory You have done this.

**6:17** For You have created the righteous and the wicked [...] from the womb You have appointed them.

**6:18** For the time of good-pleasure and the testimony of [...] You have prepared them from eternity.

**6:19** Before You created them You knew their deeds for ever and ever.

**6:20** And apart from Your will nothing is done, and nothing is known without Your good-pleasure.

**6:21** You have formed every spirit and their [...] and the judgment of all their deeds You have established.

**6:22** You have spread the heavens for Your glory, and all their host You have appointed at Your good-pleasure.

**6:23** And the mighty spirits according to their laws, before they became Your holy angels.

**6:24** And the eternal spirits in their dominions, the luminaries for their mysteries, the stars for their courses.

**6:25** And all the storm-winds for their functions, the lightning-bolts and thunders for their office.

**6:26** And the treasuries of the deeps for their purpose, and the storehouses of [...] for their [...]

**6:27** You have created the earth by Your power, the seas and the deeps.

**6:28** And [...] You have established by Your wisdom, and all that is in them You have appointed at Your good-pleasure.

**6:29** And the spirit of man that You have formed in the world for all the ages of eternity.

**6:30** And the eternal generations to [...] in their appointed times.

**6:31** And You have assigned their works in all their generations and judgment in its seasons.

**6:32** For all the ages of eternity [...] and You have appointed it for them in the wisdom of Your knowledge.

**6:33** And before they existed You knew their works, and nothing is done apart from Your will.

**6:34** And it is You who have made all knowledge, and all that exists is by Your good-pleasure.

**6:35** And there is none other to oppose Your counsel, or to understand all Your holy purpose.

**6:36** Or to gaze into the depth of Your mysteries, or to comprehend all Your wonders.

**6:37** Together with the might of Your power, and who can bear Your glory?

---

*EMET notes: Column 6 is well-preserved and contains a dual-themed hymn: personal deliverance (6:1-13) and predestinarian theology (6:14-37). The "strong tower" and "high wall" metaphors (6:4) are reminiscent of Proverbs 18:10. The deterministic theology (6:17-21) — God creating both righteous and wicked "from the womb" — is a hallmark of Qumran thought. "Holy spirit" (ruach qodshekha, 6:1) is notable as a pre-Christian use of the phrase.*
